customManagers.description: A database image pinned in a workflow's `docker run` is invisible to every built-in manager: the github-actions manager reads `uses:`, `container:` and `services:`, and the image here is an operand inside a `run:` shell block. Without this the docker-compose manager moved docker-compose.yaml alone and check-compose-image-pins.sh failed on the bot's own pull request, because that gate requires every Compose pin to be pinned by a workflow too -- a tag no workflow pins is a tag nothing tests. The marker comment names the image explicitly and sits directly above its own `docker run`, which is what ties the captured tag to it: Renovate evaluates these with RE2, which has no backreferences, so `\k<depName>` fails to compile and stops the bot outright (stokaro/ptah#2339). Proximity plus a lazy gap reaches the first image-shaped token after the marker, and requiring that token to START WITH A LETTER is what keeps it off the `--publish 26257:26257` line one row above -- a published port is digits, and it was the reason the tie had to be exact in the first place. Grouped with the compose bump by the database-server-images rule below, which matches on the same depName, so both pins move in one pull request and the gate is green on arrival.

The Spanner emulator is pinned twice: the workflow that starts the container, and the matrix cell in internal/capabilityprobe/cells.go. The cell is a Go string literal no built-in manager sees, so a bump moved the workflow alone and left the cell behind, which is what stokaro/ptah#3027 repaired. ONLY THAT ONE IMAGE IS MANAGED, and the repository is named here rather than matched by shape. Every other Image in that file carries a release LINE as its tag -- tagPinsLine in matrix.go requires tag == Line -- so the tag is an identity, not a version to keep current. A manager that matched them all bumped four of them in stokaro/ptah#3031: two ClickHouse lines were collapsed onto one image, the 26.3 and 25.8 LTS lines stopped being covered at all, and the MariaDB 11.4 cell started claiming the 11.8 cell's image. The Spanner cell is the only one declared Versionless, meaning its tag names no line, which is what makes it the only one safe to move. The pattern is RE2, which has no backreferences (stokaro/ptah#2339). Grouped with the workflow bump by the database-server-images rule below, which matches the same depName, so both pins move in one pull request.

packageRules.description: The Go toolchain is declared once, as the `toolchain` directive in go.mod, and the built-in gomod manager proposes bumps for it without configuration. There is deliberately no customManager for a Go version: the one that used to live here could only reach .golangci.yml (its second file pattern, go/.golangci.yml, never existed), so a golang bump moved that file alone while fifteen other declarations stayed behind. The `go` directive is a published compatibility floor for two separately released import paths and moves on a human decision, not a bot's.

A database server image is not an ordinary dependency. Its tag names a release LINE this repository declares in internal/capabilityprobe/cells.go, carrying a capability preset, a support level and -- for a certified line -- a compatibility commitment, so replacing a tag can retire coverage rather than update a dependency. Classify the release before merging. A new LTS or stable line is a candidate for an additional cell, not a replacement for an existing one. A new innovation or current line is an early-signal target. A patch inside a line the matrix already declares is an ordinary update. A line reaching upstream end-of-life is a support-level decision -- legacy-tested if it is worth keeping as a regression sentinel, retired if it is not -- and never an automatic removal, because upstream end-of-life is not Ptah incompatibility. Never auto-merge one of these, and never let a newer image displace a declared line without deciding what happens to that line's cell. TestRenovate_ClassifiesEveryDatabaseServerImage keeps this package list and the declared cells in step.

The clickhouse-legacy integration service is pinned below 24.11 deliberately: CHECK GRANT catalog visibility arrived in 24.11, and TestWriterDropDatabaseRealm_RejectsLegacyServerLive proves the realm-drop guard fails closed without it. Matching on the current value freezes only that pin and leaves the current clickhouse service free to update.

Every Image in internal/capabilityprobe/cells.go names the release LINE the cell reproduces -- tagPinsLine in matrix.go requires tag == Line -- so moving one is not an update. It renames the line and stops covering the old one. stokaro/ptah#3031 moved four before anyone noticed: two ClickHouse cells were collapsed onto one image, the 26.3 and 25.8 LTS lines stopped being covered, and the MariaDB 11.4 cell claimed the 11.8 cell's image; stokaro/ptah#3034 would have taken mysql 8.4 to 26.7 and postgres 13 to 18. The custom manager above is already narrowed to the one image that may move, and this rule is the second lock, on a different axis: the file is denied by name and the emulator is the single exception. The emulator is the only cell declared Versionless, meaning its tag names no line, which is what makes it safe to follow. TestRenovate_DisablesEveryLinePinnedImage requires this rule to exist, because a lock nobody checks is a lock somebody deletes.

go.mod carries two Go versions with different lifecycles. `toolchain` is what CI builds with and moves on every patch release, so Renovate keeps proposing it -- stokaro/ptah#2732 is one such bump and they are welcome. The `go` directive is the published compatibility floor: go.5x5.cz/ptah is a released import path, so raising it forces every consumer onto a newer language version, and AGENTS.md says it moves on a human decision. Renovate moved it once, in stokaro/ptah#223, under the title `update dependency go`, which reads like any other bump. The two are separable only by depType, so that is what this matches: `golang` is the directive and `toolchain` is the directive below it. Disabling the first leaves the second flowing. TestRenovate_LeavesTheCompatibilityFloorToAHuman requires this rule to exist.
